intro: Canva for social media managers on Mac is the desktop app from the Mac App Store, used for post graphics, resizing and scheduling. Scheduling needs a paid plan, and the Content Planner has limits you should know before you build a calendar. This page covers setup, the scheduler limits that catch people out, and where Lazur helps while you design.
tldr: Canva on Mac needs macOS 13.0 or later. The Mac App Store listing showed version 1.127.0 at the time we checked.
Free accounts cannot schedule. Scheduling needs Pro, Business, Education or Nonprofit access.
The Content Planner caps Instagram at 25 scheduled posts per rolling 24 hours and 20 hashtags per caption.
Editing a scheduled post pauses it, so finish the design before you queue it.
Lazur points, guides, explains and drafts while you work in Canva. It does not click buttons for you.

blocks.text: What Canva on Mac is for, and what it is not

Canva on Mac is a design app first. For a social media manager it does three jobs well: templates for post graphics, a resize tool for other platforms, and the Content Planner for queuing posts. Most of your time goes to the first two. The scheduler matters once the design is final.

Canva reported more than 265 million monthly active users and 31 million paid users at the end of 2025, according to Wikipedia. Your audience has probably seen Canva designs before. Your edge is the process around the design, not the tool.
Use Canva for the graphics. Use your own content calendar for strategy. If you keep those two jobs separate, you stop expecting a design app to plan your month.
Install the Mac app and check your macOS version
Get Canva from the Mac App Store. The listing names Canva as the developer and shows version 1.127.0 at the time we checked. It says the app requires macOS 13.0 or later.

Check your Mac before you install. Open Apple menu > About This Mac and confirm your macOS version. One search result cited macOS 12.0 for a different Canva listing, so trust the page you see on your own Mac.

The iPhone app runs on a different version track. Its App Store listing showed 4.234.0 at the same check. A phone changelog does not describe the Mac app, so read the Mac listing when you want release notes.
Set up your brand assets once, then reuse them

Before you design a single post, save the parts that never change. That means your logo, your brand colours, your fonts and a short list of photo styles. Canva keeps these in a brand kit, so each new post starts from your look, not from a blank page.
Keep one clean logo file with a transparent background. Do not keep several copies with different sizes and edges. The copy you grab first is often the wrong one.
Write your brand rules in a short text note too. Include the exact hashtag set, the words you never use, and your sign-off line. Paste from that note instead of rebuilding the same lines each week.
Resize Canva designs for Instagram and other platforms
Build the master in the format you post most, usually the feed size. Then use Resize to make the other formats from that master. The message stays the same, and you skip rebuilding text by hand.
Resize is fast, but it is not perfect. Text can shrink, wrap or move past a safe edge. Zoom in on each copy before you schedule it. A quick check beats a correction after a post goes live.

Worked example. You have a product launch post built for Instagram. Press ⌘ D to duplicate it. Rename the copy with its platform, such as launch LinkedIn, so you can find it later. Resize that copy, then move the headline away from the edges. Repeat for each platform. Each copy gets its own pass, so a fix on one does not break another.
The common mistake is fixing a size after the post is already queued. Finish every format before you open the scheduler. Then schedule once.
Scheduling in Canva: Content Planner, plan limits and costs

Scheduling is the feature that most often pushes people to pay. Free accounts cannot schedule posts. Postory says scheduling needs Pro, Business, Education or Nonprofit access. Check your plan before you build a calendar around it.

blocks.text: Prices conflict between sources. Budgetpixel lists Pro at US$18 per month or US$144 per year for one person. Postory lists US$180 per year for Pro in an article dated April 24, 2026. Check canva.com/pricing for your country before you budget.
Business replaced Teams for new buyers in late 2025. Existing Teams subscribers keep their plan. If you manage a team, confirm which plan the account is on before you invite anyone.
The limits that catch people out

items: Instagram: up to 25 scheduled posts in a rolling 24-hour window (Postory).
Instagram captions: 20 hashtags at most (Postory).
Hashtags go in the caption only (Ivory Mix). Keep your hashtag sets in a text note, then paste them in.
One platform per design (Postory). A post for LinkedIn and Instagram needs two designs or two exports.
Carousels, Stories, IGTV and Reels are not in the planner (Ivory Mix). Use another route for those formats.
Threads, Bluesky and TikTok are not supported. YouTube is publish-only (Postory).
Editing a scheduled post pauses it, and you must schedule it again (Ivory Mix).

blocks.text: The sources disagree about the full platform list. One help snippet names X, LinkedIn and Pinterest. Trust the list inside your own account, and check it before you promise a client a channel.
Ivory Mix's review has no visible date. Its image paths suggest it was written around 2021, so its limits may be out of date. Treat its list as a starting point, not a final answer.

Worked example. You want the same launch on Instagram and LinkedIn on one day. Schedule the Instagram version first, then check how much room the 24-hour window still has. Build the LinkedIn version from its own design and schedule it. Edit neither post after you queue it.
Mistakes that waste time in Canva

items: Editing after scheduling. The post pauses and waits for you. Finish the design first, then schedule.
Writing captions inside the design file. Write captions in a text note or your notes app instead. You can change a caption without touching the artwork.
Planning on the free plan. You only find the limit at the end of the week. Test the scheduler on your paid plan before a launch.
Trusting old tutorials. Limits change, so a guide from years back can send you the wrong way.
Expecting a design app to run the calendar. Canva makes the graphics. Your calendar still needs a plan.

blocks.text: Background removal, AI tools and Affinity on Mac

A December 2025 Mac App Store reviewer says background removal is limited to Pro users. The same reviewer objects to subscription costs. If your week depends on cut-outs, check which tools your plan includes before you commit.

Canva also relaunched Affinity on October 31, 2025, as one free app for Mac and Windows. It combines the former Designer, Photo and Publisher apps and needs a Canva account. AI tools such as Generative Fill and Remove Background are for premium subscribers, according to MacRumors.
Affinity is a design app, not the Content Planner. If you want to schedule, you still need Canva's scheduler or another tool. Do not look for the calendar inside Affinity.
Video and audio: where the work gets harder

Social Media Examiner's 2025 report page says 46% of marketers name video as their most important content type. Video is where a design-only workflow starts to strain. Plan short clips early, and check how each one will publish before you commit to a series.

A 2023 Mac App Store review reports audio uploads that do not play, with error messages that change. Test one clip and one music track before you build a series around them. The reviewer said email-only support did not solve it, so check the help page first.
Where Lazur fits while you work in Canva
Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on screen, and Lazur answers out loud. It looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut.
Lazur does not click buttons, edit your files or run Canva for you. It points, guides, explains and drafts. These three moves fit this job.

items: Point: ask where the Resize button is. Lazur draws a circle and a label around it on your screen.
Guide: ask for the scheduling steps. Lazur gives one step, waits for your click, then gives the next.
Draft: ask for caption options for a carousel slide. Lazur types the drafts as text you can edit.

blocks.text: Dictate captions with fn instead of typing them

Hold fn to dictate. Lazur turns your speech into clean, formatted text at the cursor, in any app. That covers a Canva text box, a caption field or a notes file. Dictation is unlimited on Pro and Power plans.

Add brand names, product names and common hashtags to the personal dictionary. Dictation then gets them right the first time. Use snippets for lines you paste every week, such as your standard link or sign-off.
A common mistake is dictating a whole week in one long take. Dictate one caption, read it back, then move on. Short takes give cleaner text and fewer fixes.
Why this job is hard: the numbers behind the workload

HubSpot's 2026 report surveyed more than 1,100 social media professionals. It finds 45% say consistently producing high-quality content is their top challenge. Metricool's 2026 well-being survey found that one in three rated their well-being negatively.

Metricool also reports that three in four feel they wear too many hats at once. It says generating new content ideas is one of the most cited sources of pressure. Both surveys come from companies that sell marketing software, so read them as signals, not proof.
A weekly Canva routine on a Mac
This routine keeps design and scheduling apart. It works for one person who manages a few accounts.

items: Early in the week, list post ideas in a text note. Dictate them with fn, one idea per line.
Build the master designs from your brand kit. Keep each campaign in its own folder.
Resize for each platform. Zoom in on every copy before you move on.
Write captions in your notes app. Paste them into the planner and count the hashtags.
Schedule the finished set, one platform per design, and stay under the Instagram window.
On Friday, check the queue. Then ask Lazur what you did last week, since its memory stays on your Mac.

blocks.text: Quick checks before you schedule

items: Read the caption in the planner, not in the design file.
Count the hashtags. Instagram captions allow 20 at most.
Confirm the time zone on the account before you set the time.
Open the preview and look for text cut off at the edges.
Check the platform list in your own account, not in an old guide.

Start with [the Lazur download](/download) and try it on a live design. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask where the Resize button is. Compare plans on [the pricing page](/pricing) once you know which features you need. If you also run campaigns for clients, read [Canva for marketers on Mac](/for/marketers/canva).

faq.question: Is Canva on Mac free for social media managers?
faq.answer: You can design for free, but free accounts cannot schedule posts. Postory says scheduling needs Pro, Business, Education or Nonprofit access. Prices vary by country, so check canva.com/pricing before you pay.

faq.question: Which macOS version does Canva for Mac need?
faq.answer: The Mac App Store listing says Canva requires macOS 13.0 or later. It showed version 1.127.0 at the time we checked. Confirm your version under Apple menu > About This Mac before you install.

faq.question: Can Canva schedule Instagram Reels or carousels?
faq.answer: Ivory Mix's review says the Content Planner does not include carousels, Stories, IGTV or Reels. The review has no visible date, so confirm the current list in your account before you plan a series.

faq.question: How many Instagram posts can Canva schedule in one go?
faq.answer: Postory lists a cap of 25 scheduled posts in a rolling 24-hour window for Instagram. Spread large batches across days so you stay under that cap.

faq.question: Why did my scheduled post stop after I edited it?
faq.answer: Editing a scheduled post pauses it, according to Ivory Mix. You then need to schedule it again. Finish the design first, then schedule once.

faq.question: Can Canva schedule to Threads, Bluesky or TikTok?
faq.answer: Postory says no for all three. It also says YouTube is publish-only. Help snippets disagree on the wider list, so check the platform list inside your own account.

faq.question: Does Lazur edit my Canva designs for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points at things, guides you one click at a time, and drafts or types text. It does not click buttons or operate Canva for you.

faq.question: Is Affinity the same as Canva's scheduler?
faq.answer: No. Affinity is a separate design app that Canva relaunched as one free app for Mac and Windows on October 31, 2025. The Content Planner is not part of Affinity.
